top_choice_rationale: P001 (Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn, B001) is a mature measurement advance of about thirty years. It solved the problem of endogenous prices and heterogeneous substitution, which allowed counterfactuals on markups, mergers and welfare that earlier approaches could not give. It has changed practice in merger review and regulation and has spread into trade, health and environmental economics. Credit is compact, since the 1995 paper is jointly authored by the three named laureates, and a method-level citation on demand estimation and market power avoids claiming the wider programme. The costs are the exclusion of Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin, and the sensitivity of applied estimates to instruments, functional form and numerical implementation, so the citation should not overstate precision. These costs do not outweigh the case for an award, so P001 ranks above no award (P000). My evidence on adoption and sensitivity is background knowledge from the round-2 exchange and I have not independently verified it.
recusal_note: No tie to Pakes, Berry or Levinsohn is apparent from the profile. Disclosed, not adjudicated: I co-authored with committee colleagues John Hassler (chair) and Tore Ellingsen (IJIO 2026), and I am married to Magdalena Andersson, a Swedish politician. The profile shows no evidence that either bears on this prize. My field, industrial organisation and international trade, is close to B001, and Hassler also supports B001, so our agreement is not independent confirmation.
